text:
ria: Heads-up — ran into a weird failure after installing the MSI on a corp laptop: redwoodctl immediately errors with \"failed to lock profiles store\" and exits.

omar: yikes. which Windows version? and was Defender active?

ria: Windows 11, Defender on. Defender quarantined redwoodctl.exe as PUA:InstallerStub. Installer still wrote C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles.json but redwoodctl couldn't create the lock in Program Files.

chris: that matches a gap in installer assumptions. Lock files should live somewhere writable by the service/user — Program Files is read-only for non-admins and can be removed by AV quarantines.

ria: log snippet from %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Temp:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:43Z INFO writing profiles to C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles.json
2026-03-18T09:12:43Z ERROR failed to acquire lock on C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\profiles.lock: access denied
2026-03-18T09:12:43Z FATAL cannot initialize profiles store: open C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe: no such file or directory
```

omar: two quick mitigations for customers: 1) Install per-user: `msiexec /i redwoodctl.msi ALLUSERS=2` which installs in %LOCALAPPDATA% and avoids Program Files locks. 2) Migrate profiles from ProgramData to %APPDATA% and set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR env var.

chris: also for the sample app (nlu-demo) note: it looks in %USERPROFILE%\\.redwood by default. If the CLI was installed machine-wide and the profiles live in ProgramData, the sample app won't find them. Add a README tip.

install-bot: Known issue recorded: INST-805 windows msi: lock path uses Program Files; conflict with AV and non-admin perms. Suggested fix: use %PROGRAMDATA% for persistent store + per-user fallback; add post-install advisory.

ria: another UX problem: when localserve tries to spawn redwoodctl for auth and the exe is quarantined the error bubbled up as a generic \"auth failed\" with zero details. lost time debugging. we should detect spawn ENOENT/EPERM and show a clear message pointing at possible AV quarantine or missing install.

omar: yes. recommend adding a preflight check on startup: run `redwoodctl --version` and if it fails, print actionable steps (msiexec ALLUSERS=2 or set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR) and link to docs.

chris: temporary doc snippet for onboarding (copy into quickstart):
```
# Windows - troubleshooting
If you see \"failed to lock profiles store\":
1) Try per-user install:
   msiexec /i redwoodctl.msi ALLUSERS=2
2) Or migrate machine profiles to user dir and set env var:
   set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=%APPDATA%\\Redwood
   redwoodctl config migrate --from C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood
3) If Defender quarantined the binary, check quarantine history or add an exclusion for C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe (orgs may require security approval).
```

devex-bot: PR created: docs/windows-install-lock-fallback (refs INST-805). Assigned to @install-team.

ria: thanks — that will help interns and new hires avoid the trap. closing once PR merges. :raised_hands:
